newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss court rules Rwandan may face U.N. tribunal.
newsitem.headline: Swiss court rules Rwandan may face U.N. tribunal.

text.p: The Swiss Federal Court has ruled that a Rwandan wanted on genocide charges can be sent to an international war crimes tribunal in Tanzania, a Justice Ministry spokesman said on Thursday.
The Lausanne-based court rejected an appeal by former tea factory director Alfred Musema to stay in Switzerland, where he had sought asylum before being taken into custody in 1995.
Musema has been indicted by the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda which was set up to try leaders of the 1994 genoicide by Hutus of up to one million Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
The U.N. tribunal, which sits in the Tanzanian city of Arusha, has indicted Musema on charges of genocide and crimes against humanity.
The spokesman said the date for Musema's transfer was not being made public for security reasons.
He added the decision was considered as compliance with a "transfer" request rather than a formal extradition, because it was in response to the tribunal rather than a government.
